newsitem.title: USA: Six-person jury chosen in secondhand-smoke trial. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Six-person jury chosen in secondhand-smoke trial. [CORRECTED 18:00 GMT]

text.p: Four women and two men were chosen on Wednesday as the jury to hear a $5 billion secondhand-smoke case brought by thousands of flight attendants' against nine tobacco defendants, the first of its kind in the United States.
(Corrects to clarify lawsuit is against nine defendants, but only seven tobacco companies).
Ten alternate jurors still had to be selected in Dade County Court, where opening arguments and testimony in the landmark case is scheduled to begin on Monday.
Judge Robert Kaye immediately swore in the jurors, who were not identified, and told them to return Monday.

After five weeks of questioning by lawyers to identify 119 potential jurors, the panel of six was chosen in just over two hours, with opposing lawyers excercising fewer than two dozen juror challenges they did not have to explain. Each side could have barred as many as 27 people without giving a reason.

The flight attendants, all non-smokers with tobacco-related sicknesses, are suing seven tobacco companies and two industry groups for $5 billion. They claim their ailments were caused by passengers' cigarette smoke aboard U.S. airlines before in-flight smoking was banned in 1988.
